plaintext.source: Szilágyi, Erdély és az északkeleti háború I (Budapest 1890) p. 393, note to letter d): 'A titkos jegyekkel írt utóírás így hangzik: nihil certius, quam Poloniam periisse, et papatum in illa'; repeated by Patera, Jana Amosa Komenského korrespondence (Praha 1892) p. 182, footnote *: 'Značí: Poloniam periisse et papatum in illa.' Covers the sentence after the signature, not the word (iyy). The key itself is printed in MHH Diplomataria XXIII (1874) p. 740 as the secret script of Rákóczi's envoys Harsányi and Balogh.

transcription.source: Page images of both prints on archive.org (bub_gb_xnVMAAAAYAAJ leaf n204; okmnytriirkczyg01gygoog leaf n235); the manuscript was not seen
transcription.notes: Printed type. The archive.org OCR misreads the digits ('(>i) (555'); corrected from the images. Counted by hand: 29 cipher letters and digits in the sentence, 3 in (iyy). Review 27 Oct 2026: the digits 6, 9, 5 (= i, n, l) are not in the printed table, where i, n, l are b, q, h; probably the printer's reading of handwritten b, q, h (hypothesis; both prints have the digits).

system.summary: Document A: reciprocal letter substitution, the Rákóczi envoys' table printed in MHH XXIII p. 740 (a=m, b=i, c=p ...), word division kept, 'et' in clear; the printed text also has the digits 6, 9, 5 for i, n, l (probably misread b, q, h); document B: system unknown.
system.notes: System fields describe document A. Review 27 Oct 2026: the table is printed in MHH Diplomataria XXIII (1874) p. 740 ('A Harsányi és Balogh Máté által használt titkos írás kulcsa'): reciprocal, a=m b=i c=p d=u,f e=g f=v g=e h=l i=b k=x l=h m=a n=q o=y p=c q=n r=z s=t t=s u=d,f x=k y=o z=r v,w=f; all 12 letter values rebuilt from the 4 Aug crib agree. The digit homophones 6=i, 9=n, 5=l are not in the printed table and are probably misreadings of handwritten b, q, h. One letter of CmCasda breaks a=m (strict decryption 'papmtum'). Document B does not decrypt with the printed table, its pairs, or the table combined with Caesar shifts.

prior_solution.where: Szilágyi, Erdély és az északkeleti háború I (1890) p. 393 and Patera 1892 p. 182: decipherment of the 4 Aug 1655 sentence only; the key printed in MHH XXIII (1874) p. 740. MHH XXIII prints both passages without decipherment; nothing for 24 May anywhere.

solution.what: Patera 1892 nos. CLI-CLV and MHH XXIII (1874) found on archive.org. Patera prints the 4 Aug 1655 cipher sentence with a footnote decipherment (p. 182); MHH prints the same cipher without one. The 24 May passage has no decipherment in either.
Both cipher passages and the word (iyy) read from the page images of both prints; OCR errors in the digits and in 'Gpdlmuoyqnotlses' corrected; variant Xyopatus / Xyoapus recorded.

Key rebuilt from Patera's plaintext (check.py): 15 sign values, digit homophones 6=i, 5=l, 9=n. It decrypts the sentence as 'poloniam periisse et papmtum in illa': one conflict, the 4th letter of CmCasda (cipher a, elsewhere plain m), which Patera reads as plain a.
Shuffled key and letters shuffled inside each word both give gibberish (check.py, seed 1).

Independent re-check by a second agent: own downloads of the four page images, own key script, readings of both cipher lines confirmed; found the CmCasda conflict and the page number (p. 182, not 181).
24 May passage: the 4 Aug key, its inverse, the pairs as a reciprocal table, and the pairs combined with Caesar shifts on 22-26 letter alphabets. No Latin.
24 May passage: Caesar, affine and progressive shifts; Vigenère, Beaufort and Porta with about 10,000 Latin keywords from Patera's text and names (Schaum, Comenius, Rakoczi ...). No Latin.

24 May passage: annealing of a one-to-one letter substitution with word division kept (anneal.py). Matched control: the same annealer recovers two synthetic Latin texts of 56 and 50 letters exactly. On the 24 May passage only nonsense optima. So it is not a simple substitution of Latin with this word division.

Context in the same correspondence, checked on the page images of Patera (leaves n200-n205): CLI (20 May) 'legantur ... eo modo, quo Schaumiana legi necesse est ex pacto' (OCR only); CLII (24 May) the cipher follows news quoted from a letter from England and precedes a P.S. and the closing on p. 179; CLIII (22 Jul) 'Addo occultiora pagina sequenti, carbo ostendet' (in italic; invisible ink, not printed); CLV (6 Sept) italic passages with note * on p. 183: 'Co ležatým písmem vytištěno, psáno v originále tajným písmem', and 'Occulta scriptura nihil scribo hac vice'.

Review pass: the cipher lines, the word (iyy) and the 22 Jul and 6 Sept passages re-checked on the page images; found that the 6 Sept letter's secret passages are printed in clear (Patera p. 183 note *), correcting the first report that it has no secret text, and that the 24 May cipher is not at the end of the letter.

Review: check.py re-run; the rebuilt key decrypts the sentence as 'poloniam periisse et papmtum in illa', one conflict (4th letter of CmCasda, cipher a = plain m elsewhere); both prints re-checked on the page images, both have 'a'.

Review: MHH XXIII (1874) p. 740 (archive.org leaf n724) prints 'A Harsányi és Balogh Máté által használt titkos írás kulcsa', a reciprocal table a=m b=i c=p d=u,f e=g f=v g=e h=l i=b k=x ...; all 12 letter values rebuilt from the 4 Aug crib agree (check.py, 12 of 12). The reciprocal guess is confirmed; Comenius used the Rákóczi court table.

Review: the digits 6=i, 9=n, 5=l are not in the printed table, where i, n, l are b, q, h; handwritten b, q, h read as 6, 9, 5 by the printer would make '69 655m' = 'bq bhhm' and the system a plain reciprocal table. Not testable without the original.

Review: Szilágyi, Erdély és az északkeleti háború I (1890) pp. 388-394 (archive.org erdlysazsz01sziluoft): p. 393 prints the decipherment of the 4 Aug sentence (earlier than Patera 1892); p. 392 prints the first lines of the 22 Jul invisible-ink page ('Londino 4. Junii Constantinus Schaum ...'), the rest washed out; italic = secret script in the 22 Jul and 6 Sept letters, plaintext only; 24 May only referred to Okmánytár 178.

Review: siblings in Patera (register: Klobusický pp. 174, 178-183, 219; CXLVIII, CLI-CLVI) and MHH XXIII (Comenius items incl. 'Comenius incognita scriptura', invisible ink): no further letter-cipher passage.

Review: 24 May passage with the printed MHH p. 740 table ('hantkaoy ? ecuhadyonqyshtgt ...'), and the table combined with Caesar shifts on 23/25/26-letter alphabets in both orders, scored with the shared la, en-modern, de-modern, hu-modern and pl-modern models: best -4.9 per character against -1.7 for the 4 Aug plaintext.

Review: anneal_lm.py, one-to-one substitution scored with the shared Latin model la (5-grams with spaces) plus word bonus; matched control (56 letters, 17 signs) recovered exactly; 24 May gives nonsense at -3.1 to -3.5 per character.

Review: anneal_lm.py --long, homophonic substitution with letters and digits as signs (the 4 Aug system as printed); the matched control (66 signs, 23 distinct) is not recovered with 60 restarts x 20,000 steps, so the 24 May optima are uninformative (underdetermined).
Review: reading of the 4 Aug sentence re-read as Latin and graded A; documents[B].language set to 'unknown' and the 'la' dropped from its text entry (no plaintext language established).

outcome.method_basis: The 4 Aug 1655 sentence is deciphered in print, first by Szilágyi (1890, p. 393), then by Patera (1892, p. 182); here the cipher was transcribed from both prints, the key rebuilt from the decipherment and found to agree with the Rákóczi table printed in MHH XXIII (1874) p. 740, one letter in conflict. The 24 May 1655 passage is not deciphered.

outcome.notes: Catalogue 474. Of the four letters: 24 May has a printed cipher passage (not deciphered); 4 Aug has a printed cipher sentence (deciphered in print by Szilágyi 1890 and Patera 1892) and the cipher word (iyy); 22 Jul has secret-script phrases printed in clear in italic and an invisible-ink page of which Szilágyi 1890 printed the first lines (the rest illegible); 6 Sept has secret-script passages printed in clear in italic. The key of the 4 Aug sentence is the Rákóczi envoys' reciprocal table printed in MHH XXIII (1874) p. 740. Written up 27 Oct 2026 after a review pass.

texts.label: A, 4 Aug 1655 (Patera CLIV p. 182; MHH XXIII no. CXXIX p. 219; Szilágyi 1890 p. 393)
texts.summary: Comenius, writing from Leszno during the Swedish invasion of Poland, ends his report to Rákóczi's councillor Klobusiczky with one ciphered sentence: 'Nothing is more certain than that Poland has perished, and the papacy in it.' The letter around it reports the Swedish advance from Poznań on Warsaw and the flight of the Catholic clergy. Comenius was then pressing George II Rákóczi of Transylvania to side with Sweden (background, not taken from this letter).

reading_review.note: Read as Latin: 'Nihil certius quam Poloniam periisse, et papatum in illa' is a complete, grammatical sentence (accusative and infinitive after 'certius quam') and fits the letter's report of the Swedish conquest of Great Poland and the flight of the Catholic clergy. It rests on the printed decipherment (Szilágyi 1890, Patera 1892); the decoder gives 'papmtum' at one letter. The second sentence is clear Latin with one unread word, (iyy). 19 of 20 words read.

texts.note: Decipherment from Szilágyi 1890 p. 393 and Patera 1892 p. 182 note *, checked letter by letter with the key rebuilt from it (python check.py), which is the table printed in MHH XXIII p. 740.

texts.label: B, 24 May 1655 (Patera CLII p. 178; MHH XXIII no. CIII p. 178)
texts.summary: The cipher stands in a letter in which Comenius quotes news from a friend in England (23 Apr 1655): Schaum has not yet arrived there, the Polish and Swedish envoys in London, the Waldensian massacre in Piedmont, the fleet in America. The cipher follows this news and comes before a postscript ('Tandem apulit [...] dominus Schaum') that seems to belong to the same English letter; the letter then goes on and closes 'Raptissime 24 Maji 1655'. The cipher itself is not deciphered.
texts.note: Not deciphered. The decryption file records the failed trials (4 Aug key and the printed MHH p. 740 table, inverse, shifts; annealing with matched controls), not a reading. Plaintext language not established.
